ety.text: Borrowed from French nitrogène (coined by French chemist and physician Jean-Antoine Chaptal in 1790). By surface analysis, nitro- + -gen. See also niter.

senses.d: The chemical element (symbol N) with an atomic number of 7 and atomic weight of 14.0067. It is a colorless and odorless gas.
ex: By molar fraction, nitric oxide contains equal parts nitrogen and oxygen.

senses.d: Molecular nitrogen (diatomic nitrogen), N₂, a colorless, odorless gas at room temperature, which constitutes most of air (78% of it).
ex: The air you breathe is mostly nitrogen.

senses.d: A specific nitrogen atom within a chemical formula, or a specific isotope of nitrogen.
ex: The two nitrogens are located next to one another on the ring.

ety.text: From Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “not”) + ζωή (zōḗ, “life”), coined by Antoine Lavoisier.
Borrowed from French nitrogène, coined by Lavoiser. By surface analysis, nitro- + -geno.

pt:nitrogênio.gl: Brazilian Portuguese standard spelling of nitrogénio

syn: E941 when used as a packaging gas
